picks.reasoning: CBLOL is 0-3 against the LCK this year, and LCK has won 10 of the last 13 Worlds titles while CBLOL has never reached a final. T1's recent form is ugly, but their players are the better individuals and they have the bigger stage history, so I'm not buying the LOS hype.

LOS owns the early tempo on paper: 70% first towers, +0.8k at 15, and a 45% first blood rate, while T1 is -0.8k at 15 and only 40% first towers. But CBLOL is 0-3 against the LCK this year, the LCK holds 68% against other regions to CBLOL's 36%, and T1 are the reigning world champions who won 6 titles and reached the EWC final. Region strength outweighs LOS's early lead, so I'm taking T1 to close out the tempo fight.

CBLOL went 0-3 against the LCK in 2026 and the LCK holds 68% against other regions to CBLOL's 36%, with the last ten Worlds titles going to the LCK, so T1's international edge is decisive for me. T1's recent form (LWLWLWLLLW) and their 9-11 record over the last 20 games are real concerns, but their draft depth on Fearless and Keria's steadiness should carry them past a region that has not beaten the LCK this year.

CBLOL is 0-3 against the LCK in 2026 and only 36% against other regions versus the LCK's 68%, and T1 are the reigning world champions with six titles, so region strength decides this for me. LOS's 24-11 series record is built on a weaker league, and T1's recent form is shaky, so I keep the confidence measured.

LOS are riding a hot streak and have the calmer, comeback-capable group, but T1's recent slump is more about nerves than talent, and reigning champions with an LCK edge that big usually find their rhythm on the Worlds stage. I'm backing T1 to steady themselves when it matters.
